quotes.text: Automation has long existed in development, think scripts, CICD, pipelines, and templates. These are rigid by design. They follow exact instructions step by step, but they break when conditions shift unexpectedly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates traditional automation from adaptive autonomy.

quotes.text: Treat each recommendation as a draft proposal, accept the pieces that align with your standards, revise the ones that don't, and capture lessons for the next project iteration.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical guidance for keeping human judgment in agent-assisted development.

quotes.text: Human oversight doesn't vanish. Your role changes from checking boxes line by line to defining guidelines at the start, which regions are allowed, which costs are acceptable, which compliance standards can't be breached.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Describes how the operator role shifts to defining guardrails.

quotes.text: Not every agent generated test deserves to live in your permanent suite. Flaky or irrelevant tests can accumulate quickly, wasting time and undermining trust in automation. That's why governance matters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A realistic caveat about AI-generated tests.

quotes.text: Another misconception worth clearing up is the idea that agents fix bugs. They don't rewrite production code or patch flaws on their own. What they do exceptionally well is surface reproducible scenarios with clear diagnostic detail.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about what testing agents do.

chapters.title: Cloud agents running Azure on autopilot
Closing the intelligence loop in DevOps

takeaways: Agentic AI differs from autocomplete because agents keep context, memory and goals, coordinate in specialised roles and adapt when conditions change.
In .NET and Azure work, agents can scaffold projects, provision infrastructure, detect drift and generate edge-case tests, but only within guardrails that humans define and review.
Start small with one measurable pilot, such as Copilot on a prototype or a test agent against staging, and feed lessons from logs and pull requests back into the next project.
hook: DevOps teams lose hours to setup work, configuration drift and bugs that only show up in production. This episode is for .NET and Azure developers and engineering leads, explaining how agentic AI moves from autocomplete to a teammate that scaffolds, provisions, tests and remembers lessons, while humans keep control through guardrails.
